summary_html: **Educators/school staff** observing indicators of abuse/neglect report to CPS under state mandatory-reporter lists built on the federal CAPTA floor.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — requires robust reporter regimes that include education sector professionals

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that KRS 620.030(1) imposes an individual, non-delegable duty to report suspected child abuse directly to law enforcement, the Cabinet, or a prosecutor, so a teacher's and counselor's report to their school principal neither discharged that duty nor entitled them to KRS 620.050 immunity from misdemeanor prosecution.
key_cases.relevance: The case arose from school employees and squarely holds that school protocol reporting to a principal does not satisfy an educator's statutory reporting duty.
key_cases.quote: All individuals with firsthand knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that a child is abused have a mandatory duty to report the abuse.

key_cases.holding: The court remanded for the trial court to determine whether KRS 620.030's mandatory reporting duty applied to a teacher, because if it did the duty is ministerial rather than discretionary and qualified official immunity would be unavailable for her failure to report a student's alleged sexual assault.
key_cases.relevance: It arose from a school employee's response to a report of student-on-student sexual abuse and governs educator liability in Kentucky.
key_cases.quote: if the mandatory reporting laws apply, then Turner could not be afforded the protection of qualified official immunity

search_keywords: Kentucky Department for Community Based Services

state_agency.name: Kentucky Department for Community Based Services
state_agency.hotline: 1-877-597-2331 (1-877-KYSAFE1) or 1-800-752-6200; call the phone line nights, weekends and holidays - the online report form is monitored 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(1)
Physicians, osteopathic physicians, nurses, residents, interns — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Teachers and school personnel — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Social workers and child-caring personnel — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Coroners and medical examiners — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Chiropractors, dentists, optometrists — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Emergency medical technicians and paramedics — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Health professionals and mental health professionals — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Peace officers — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
Any organization or agency employing any of the above — Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(2)(a)
reporting_details: Kentucky is a universal mandatory reporting state — any person who knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a child is dependent, neglected, or abused must immediately report to a local law enforcement agency, the Department of Kentucky State Police, the cabinet or its designated representative, the Commonwealth's attorney, or the county attorney (Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 620.030(1)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 4, 24, 48, or 72 hours, or 5 working days (tiered by risk level)
